automatic_update_policy.policy: Remain exactly pinned to Lean 4.33.0 and the committed dependency revisions until one enumerated reevaluation trigger is documented and authorized.

candidate_transition_policy.active_baseline_remains_authority_until: A migration candidate closes every required source, kernel, checker, mutation, custody, documentation, and replay gate.
candidate_transition_policy.failed_candidate_disposition: Reject or archive the candidate without changing the active 4.33.0 baseline.

reevaluation_triggers.description: A security advisory or kernel-soundness issue materially affects the pinned toolchain or this repository's checked proof surface.

A capability, dependency, platform, or build route required by the maintained project scope is blocked under the pinned baseline, and no acceptable pinned-baseline workaround preserves that required scope.

The exact pinned baseline or a required exact dependency revision is sustainably and reproducibly unobtainable across the maintained official and repository-cache routes; a transient network, mirror, or host failure is insufficient.

A human maintainer creates an explicit exception record with rationale, acknowledges that a new release alone is insufficient, authorizes a reviewed migration, and requires a new versioned replay receipt before activation.

scope_boundary: This policy governs when the repository reevaluates its active Lean and Mathlib pins; it is not a claim that Lean 4.33.0 is universally preferable or permanently defect-free.
A new upstream release, elapsed time, or a desire to track latest is not by itself a reevaluation trigger.

The pin and replay establish repository-local configuration and bounded execution evidence, not publisher authentication, reproducible builds, kernel soundness, theorem intent, scientific validity, or refinement to Rust, binary64, PID estimators, data, populations, or applications.
Historical 4.32.x receipts remain versioned observations of their original bytes and must not be rewritten to appear as 4.33.0 evidence.
